articleTitle: Microwave heating
abstract: The principles of microwave heating as applied to industrial processing are outlined and the basic design of applicators for material processing is described. Industrial applications range from food tempering to rubber vulcanisation and from vacuum drying to sintering of ceramics. The most promising applications to date are summarised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical apparatus for flammable atmospheres: intrinsic safety
abstract: Intrinsic safety (IS) is defined as a protection technique based on the restriction of electrical energy to a level which is too low to be able to ignite an explosive atmosphere. The author describes some of the principles involved. It differs essentially from all other methods of protection of electrical apparatus for use in potentially explosive atmospheres because the flow of energy from the safe area must be carefully controlled. Its growth has been greatly accelerated by the development of barrier devices which protect the hazardous area from the effects of possible intrusion of dangerous sources of energy from the safe area parts of the system. In future it is possible that fibre-optic transmission of data will supersede many existing barrier applications for IS systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Regenerative equipment for railway rolling stock
abstract: The specification of railway propulsion equipment increasingly includes the requirement for regenerative braking. Both British Rail and London Underground have recently placed their first significant orders for regenerative rolling stock. The author reviews the technology of modern regenerative traction equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Widening applications for VAR compensation
abstract: The authors describe how improved techniques for controlling VAR flows can bring about further reductions in power losses and save alternative capital investment in transmission, distribution and industrial electricity supply networks. The quality of voltage provided to consumers may also be improved. They show that thyristor switching, computer control and optical communications technology all assist in these developments, but argue that they must be cost effective.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of SF/sub 6/ upon power switchgear technology. II. Switch systems implications
abstract: For pt. I see ibid., vol.4, no.5, p.215 (1990). A successful circuit breaker needs not only a suitable interrupter design but also a suitable medium in which to form and quench the arc. SF/sub 6/ is increasingly being used in circuit breakers as an alternative to oil and air. The author looks at the impact of SF/sub 6/ on switching systems including transmission switchgear and distribution switchgear. The effects on monitoring and control are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Balancing high-voltage batteries
abstract: Typically, HV standby batteries live for most of their lives on float charge, providing that all important insurance in the event of power loss. When called on to deliver power in an emergency, it is essential that, if they are to perform to expectation and provide adequate cover, they must be balanced. The author looks at the importance of ensuring that a HV battery system is balanced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric shark barrier: initial trials and prospects
abstract: A new field of application for power engineering lies in the electrical protection of bathing beaches against sharks at luxury tourist resorts. The author reviews traditional methods of protection from shark attack, then discusses the reaction of fish and sharks to pulsed electric fields. An experimental system has been installed at a bathing resort, with promising results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power system stability. II. Hardware, generators and their controls
abstract: For pt.I see ibid., vol.5, no.1, p.29-35, 1991. In this, the second part of a three-part tutorial series on the effects of electric generators on power system stability, the author examines inherent stability of the synchronous generator, looks in more detail at the generator and its controls, and introduces the equal-area criterion for salient-pole machines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power system stability. I. Fundamental theory
abstract: Our civilisation is heavily dependent on the constant and reliable availability of electrical energy, which is supplied through an interconnected power system and generated by synchronous generators. The power system and its generators must be stable, for the occasional loss of stability can be quite traumatic. The study of power systems stability is essential if it is to be retained, and such is the basis of this series of tutorials. Here, the basic theory of power system stability is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a new surge arrester technology
abstract: The authors discuss development of a new arrester that incorporates a resistance-graded series gap with MOV discs which offers several improvements over silicon carbide and gapless MOV arrester designs. The design allows the utility specifiers to substantially improve surge protection to distribution equipment, especially URD cable and overhead distribution transformers. It provides substantial improvements in temporary overvoltage withstand capabilities, which improves arrester reliability. The increased temporary overvoltage capability allows users to protect ungrounded wye-delta transformer banks without sacrificing surge protection. The unique sharing of voltage between the disc and ring/gap sections improves durability during high-current discharge testing. The ring/gap sections' overvoltage capability and the lower stress present across the MOV discs themselves under steady-rate conditions result in a reduced likelihood of initial energisation failures, which is a major concern to utility operating personnel.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of 1992 on transmission and distribution plant
abstract: The effects of 1992 are interwoven with those of privatisation. Here, the author shows how the combination will radically alter the characteristics of the power equipment market in the UK. He argues that manufacturing industry is already being shaped, and that the long-established interface between customers and suppliers will change.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of fuses to power-system equipment
abstract: The author looks at how fuselinks are used to protect separate items of equipment. Specifically the author considers cables, motors, power and voltage transformers, power capacitors and semiconductor devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technology transfer: the BTG model
abstract: Although there may be some who still think of technology transfer in terms of assistance to Third World countries, most now understand it to mean the process in a developed economy by which a business can benefit from technology transferred to it. Even so the significance of intellectual property is still not fully appreciated and often undervalued, particularly in the engineering field. The author draws attention to the opportunities which exist, the changes of attitude necessary to take advantage of them and some of the ways in which technology transfer can be achieved. It is suggested that, as the world's principal exponent of technology transfer, the British Technology Group (BTG) is a good model for all similar activities in this field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A manufacturer's view of the transmission and distribution business after 1992
abstract: This article, based on a contribution to an IEE discussion meeting, tries to predict the effect of the measures being introduced by the European Commission for the creation of the single European market on the power transmission and distribution plant business. It is an overview of the factors involved and the effects produced in a business dominated by the purchasing power of large electrical utilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of Medallion 2000 award advanced house specification
abstract: The electricity supply industry has a number of 'Medallion' award specifications covering the thermal performance of houses. The Medallion 2000 is at present the most advanced. It requires a number of features in addition to the 1990 Building Regulations. These are: double glazing in place of single glazing; a high degree of structural airtightness; and whole house mechanical ventilation with heat recovery. The '2000' specification was derived from systematic research and development, owner/occupied field trials and detailed market considerations. The author gives a general review of the work.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced package CHP unit for small-scale operation
abstract: The idea of combined heat and power has been around for a long time, but small-scale plants have only become practicable commercially in the UK during the last decade. The authors consider small systems generally, then goes on to describe the advanced package CHP system manufactured by their company.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Qualification of XLPE tube systems for cooling high-voltage high power electrical equipment
abstract: The introduction in the mid-1970s of high-voltage high-current silicon thyristors for electrical power conversion created a need for extremely reliable but economical liquid cooling systems in which purified water-based coolants could be circulated. Research and development over 2/sup 1///sub 2/ years on XLPE tube systems and compatible nonmetallic connectors has resulted in a single-circuit purified glycol/water fluid system cooling a 150 MW back-to-back HVDC link in Canada. The author discusses the system requirements, electrical stress, conductivity control, electrolysis and temperature cycles. The author then discusses the thermal cycle testing and post ageing testing of the XLPE connectors. The suitability of XLPE for the cooling system is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Management of protection
abstract: Protection is normally defined in terms of its technical performance on the power system which it protects. However, there are other aspects which are of equal importance concerning the management of protection, in terms of what has to be done, who is to do it, and its financial and operational requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power transformers-the second century
abstract: The author traces the progress of power transformer technology during its first century and looks at how such technology might develop in its second century. High reliability in service is a major requirement for power transformer design. New failure mechanisms have been identified that include part-winding resonance, fast-front transients, geomagnetic disturbances and static electrification. These new phenomena must be understood and design philosophies developed to encompass the potential problems. Progress in the second century is science based with the application of rigorous design control procedures to ensure that every innovative change is correctly reviewed to establish the pedigree of the change and foresee all possible ramifications of the change on the transformer in test or in service.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power plant operation and maintenance cost reduction through control system improvements
abstract: Since 1973, operating and maintenance costs for power production plant have increased by 410%, while fuel costs have increased by 445%. Plant automation through improved instrumentation and control systems provides a cost-effective means to contain both operating and maintenance costs, as well as assisting in the more efficient utilisation of fuel by improving plant efficiency, manoeuvrability, reliability and availability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power quality
abstract: The increasing use of power electronic convertors and controllers for industrial processes and drives, and in the home, enhances the problems of electromagnetic interference. The effects spread from power frequencies to radio frequencies, and hence such interference can be conducted via the supply system or radiated. New related standards and regulations will come into operation within the European Community from 1992.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The influence of Michael Faraday on power engineering
abstract: The author looks at the life of Michael Faraday starting when he was first introduced to science in 1811 by Sir Humphrey Davy. His influence on teaching and designing is looked at and the work he did on electrical machines is discussed in particular. Other influences on power engineering are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specifying large electrical variable-speed-drive system installations
abstract: The author reviews technical features of large variable speed drive systems and makes recommendations having regard to the economic and the technical aspects of the performance of the system, with respect to contractual pitfalls. These factors should be taken into account when users are specifying large variable speed drives and they can help purchasers to get what they ask for.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The power system for the Channel Tunnel
abstract: The Channel Tunnel Project is currently the largest construction project in Europe. Its objective is to create a fixed-link transportation system between the UK and France. Here, the author describes how the development of its power system has basically been the application of well proven and reliable technology to meet the specific and unique requirements of this project.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Genesis and evolution of advanced protection-an exercise in industrial/university co-operation (power systems)
abstract: The author traces the history of a major co-operative research and development project into power system protection involving a team of engineers from the industrial and academic worlds. It began in 1978 and has also involved the CEGB, Hydro-Quebec, Bonneville Power Administration and Hong Kong Electric. The author gives no more than a flavour of the overall activity to be given, but more detail is available in an extensive and detailed review commissioned by the IEE (see IEE Proc.C, vol.135, no.4, p.334-68, 1988).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Making better buildings and making buildings better
abstract: Based on his experience as a consulting engineer the author discusses the field of installation engineering-the utilisation of electric power within buildings. The author discusses the role of the consultant, IEE Wiring Regulations and management of the project. The author then discusses the building of the House of Fraser store in the Meadowhall complex in Sheffield, the building of a new ice rink, and the refurbishment of Broadcasting House in London. The energy requirements and power supplies for each building are discussed. The author compares European practice with that of the UK.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-aided study and design in power system engineering using personal-computer-based application software
abstract: Personal computers are increasingly playing important roles in many of our daily activities and power engineering is no exception. The author describes the application of PC-based computer-aided tools in solving some of the problems in power system engineering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overhead lines-loading and strength: the probabilistic approach viewed internationally
abstract: Recently, several countries have published documents related to the probabilistic design of overhead lines, and almost concurrently the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEG) has issued four Reports in the 826 series, representing an international concensus of opinion on this subject. The underlying principles are that neither the loads applied to an overhead line nor the strengths of the components can be described by single values, and a statistical knowledge of the loads and of the strengths is required. Any attempt at preparing a loading specification without a parallel strength specification would defeat the new approach, which permits the evaluation of relative reliabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
